data.summary: Learn why separating recyclable waste from general waste is important in Malaysia.
data.sourceName: New Straits Times: Separating waste at source to boost recycling rate
data.title: Waste Separation at Source in Malaysia
data.content:
Waste separation at source means separating recyclable waste before it is thrown away with general rubbish. In Malaysia, this practice helps reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills and supports better recycling habits among the community.

Recyclable items such as paper, cardboard, plastic bottles, metal cans, and glass should be separated from food waste and other dirty waste. When recyclable items are clean and dry, they are easier to collect, sort, and process.

This practice is important because landfill space is limited. If more recyclable materials are separated properly, less useful waste will be disposed of together with general waste.

Users can start by preparing a separate bag or container at home for recyclable items. Before sending them to a recycling bin or recycling centre, make sure the items are empty, clean, and dry.

data.summary: Understand how recycling centres support collection, sorting, and community recycling.
data.sourceName: Planning Malaysia Journal: Examining Recyclable Items Collection
data.title: How Recycling Centres Help Communities
data.content:
Recycling centres help the community manage recyclable items in a more organised way. They provide a proper place for people to send items that should not be thrown together with general waste.

In Malaysia, recycling facilities such as Material Recovery Collection Facilities and Community Recycling Centres can support the collection of recyclable items. These facilities help collect and sort materials so that recyclable waste can be managed more effectively.

Common recyclable items include paper, cardboard, plastics, metals, and glass. Some centres may also accept special items depending on their programme, so users should check the accepted item list before visiting.

Recycling centres are useful because they make recycling easier for the public. They also help reduce the amount of recyclable items that end up in landfills.
